'''Mostafa Kamal Tolba''' ({{Langx|ar|مصطفى كمال طلبة}}) (8 December 1922 – 28 March 2016) was an Egyptian scientist who served for seventeen years as the executive director of the [[United Nations Environment Programme]] (UNEP).<ref>{{cite book|title=The Environment Encyclopedia and Directory 2001|date=2001|publisher=Europa Publications|isbn=1857430891|page=545|edition=3rd}}</ref> In that capacity he led development of the [[Montreal Protocol]], which saved the [[ozone layer]] and thus millions of lives from skin cancer and other impacts.<ref name=":0" />

== Biography ==

Mustafa Kamal Tolba was born in the town of [[Zifta]] (located in [[Gharbia Governorate]]), Tolba graduated from [[Cairo University]] in 1943 and obtained a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from [[Imperial College London]] five years later. He established his own school in [[microbiology]] at Cairo University's Faculty of Science and also taught at the [[University of Baghdad]] during the 1950s. In addition to his academic career, Tolba worked in the Egyptian civil service.<ref name="UNEP">{{Cite web |url=http://ozone.unep.org/Events/awards2005_profiles.shtml |title=2005 Awards Profiles: Mostafa Kamal Tolba (Egypt) |work=The Vienna Convention Award For Outstanding Contributions to the Protection of the Ozone Layer |publisher=[[United Nations Environment Programme]] |accessdate=2010-10-08 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=http://webarchive.loc.gov/all/20150412223537/http://ozone.unep.org/Events/awards2005_profiles.shtml |archivedate=2015-04-12 }}</ref>

After serving briefly as President of the [[Egyptian Olympic Committee]] (1971–1972),<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.egolympic.org.eg/ar/president_A.pdf |title=Egyptian Olympic Committee Presidents 1910 until now |publisher=[[Egyptian Olympic Committee]] |language=Arabic |format=[[Portable Document Format|PDF]], 2.86 MB |accessdate=2010-10-07 }}{{dead link|date=November 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Tolba led Egypt's delegation to the landmark [[United Nations Conference on the Human Environment|1972 Stockholm Conference]], which established the United Nations Environment Programme. Tolba became UNEP's Deputy Executive Director immediately after the conference, and two years later was promoted to executive director.

During his long tenure as director of UNEP (1975–1992), he played a central role in the fight against [[ozone depletion]], which culminated with the [[Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer|Vienna Convention]] (1985) and the [[Montreal Protocol]] (1987).<ref name="UNEP" /><ref>{{cite news|title=Mostafa Tolba: Green giant: A creator of the successful regime to reduce global emissions has died|url=https://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21695857-creator-successful-regime-reduce-global-emissions-has-died-green-giant|accessdate=2 April 2016|newspaper=[[The Economist]]|date=2 April 2016}}</ref> He enabled these negotiations by serving as a bridge between ministers and scientists since they did not understand each others' language.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Vaughan |first=Scott |date=29 March 2016 |title=Dr. Mostafa Tolba: Architect of the Montreal Protocol, IPCC and Biodiversity Convention |url=https://www.iisd.org/publications/report/dr-mostafa-tolba-architect-montreal-protocol-ipcc-and-biodiversity-convention |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=International Institute for Sustainable Development |language=en}}</ref> He described the Montreal Protocol as a "start and strengthen" treaty, where the parties started modestly, gained the knowledge they needed to phase out the dangerous chemicals, and gained the confidence they needed to do more.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Mostafa Tolba, Father of Montreal Protocol, Dies at 93 - IGSD |date=29 March 2016 |url=https://www.igsd.org/dr-mostafa-tolba-father-of-montreal-protocol-dies-at-93/ |access-date=2023-05-21 |language=en-US}}</ref>

He successfully steered negotiations for the [[Basel Convention]] on transboundary hazardous waste.<ref name=":0" />  He was a significant influence in the creation and organization of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]], and the [[Global Environment Facility]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Bolin|first1=Bert|title=A History of the Science and Politics of Climate Change. The Role of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change|date=2007|publisher=Cambridge University Press|location=Cambridge}}</ref> He led the work to develop the [[Convention on Biological Diversity]].<ref name=":0" />

In 1982, Mostafa K. Tolba, as executive director of the United Nations environmental program, told UN delegates that if the nations of the world continued their present policies, they would face by the turn of the century <nowiki>''</nowiki>an environmental catastrophe which will witness devastation as complete, as irreversible, as any [[nuclear holocaust]].<nowiki>''</nowiki><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Shabecoff |first1=Philip |date=1982-05-11 |title=U.N. ECOLOGY PARLEY OPENS AMID GLOOM |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1982/05/11/world/un-ecology-parley-opens-amid-gloom.html |access-date=2023-02-07 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

Tolba died on 28 March 2016 in Geneva at the age of 93.<ref>{{cite news|title=Mostafa K. Tolba, U.N. environmental official, dies at 93|last=Weil|first=Martin|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/energy-environment/mostafa-k-tolba-un-environmental-official-dies-at-93/2016/03/29/e38b1e74-f558-11e5-9804-537defcc3cf6_story.html|newspaper=[[Washington Post]]|date=29 March 2016|accessdate=1 April 2016}}</ref>

==Publications==
Tolba's publications include more than 95 papers on [[plant pathology]], as well as over 600 statements and articles on the environment.<ref name="UNEP"/>
